nodes.label: Graphify Knowledge Graph Workflow
nodes.rationale: Graphify query/path/explain return a scoped subgraph, usually much smaller than GRAPH_REPORT.md or raw grep output, so agents should prefer them for codebase questions to minimize context cost.

nodes.label: graphify query command
nodes.rationale: Preferred first step for codebase questions when graphify-out/graph.json exists because it returns a scoped subgraph.

nodes.label: graphify path command
nodes.rationale: Used for exploring relationships between two entities.

nodes.label: graphify update command
nodes.rationale: Run after modifying code to keep the graph current; AST-only so it incurs no API cost.

nodes.label: GRAPH_REPORT.md
nodes.rationale: Read only for broad architecture review or when scoped queries do not surface enough context, because it is large.

nodes.label: graphify-out/wiki/index.md
nodes.rationale: Preferred over raw source browsing for broad navigation when it exists.

nodes.label: Dirty Graph Files Policy
nodes.rationale: Dirty graphify-out/ files are expected after hooks or incremental updates, so dirtiness alone must not cause an agent to skip graphify; only stale/incorrect-graph tasks or explicit user instruction justify skipping.

nodes.label: db service (pgvector/pgvector:pg16)
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL with the pgvector extension is used as the vector database for RAG embeddings; a pg_isready healthcheck gates dependent service startup.

nodes.label: api service (FastAPI backend + static web frontend)
nodes.rationale: Built from ./back, serves both the API and the static frontend on port 8000; waits for db service_healthy so it never starts against an unready database.
nodes.norm_label: api service (fastapi backend + static web frontend)

nodes.label: postgres_data volume
nodes.rationale: Named volume persisting /var/lib/postgresql/data so embeddings survive container recreation.

nodes.label: DATABASE_URL configuration
nodes.rationale: Uses the compose service name 'db' as host so the API resolves the database over the compose network rather than localhost.

nodes.label: OLLAMA_HOST configuration
nodes.rationale: Defaults to http://host.docker.internal:11434 so the containerized API can reach an Ollama LLM running on the host machine.

nodes.label: GEMINI_API_KEY configuration
nodes.rationale: Passed through from the host environment rather than baked in, keeping the secret out of the compose file.

nodes.label: connection status indicator
nodes.rationale: status-dot/status-text start as 'Connecting...' so the UI reflects backend reachability before the first request.

nodes.label: memory indicator and Clear memory button
nodes.rationale: Conversation memory is exposed and resettable in the UI so users can control the context carried between turns.
nodes.norm_label: memory indicator and clear memory button

nodes.label: settings sidebar (model, system prompt, temperature, stream)
nodes.rationale: Exposes model selection with a custom-name override, a system prompt that overrides the default RAG prompt, temperature and streaming toggle, making the app a hands-on RAG experimentation surface rather than a fixed chatbot.
nodes.norm_label: settings sidebar (model, system prompt, temperature, stream)

nodes.label: Request payload preview
nodes.rationale: Renders the outgoing request JSON in a collapsed <details> block so users can see exactly what the settings produce — a learning/debugging affordance.

nodes.label: TMDB retrieval-augmented answering
nodes.rationale: The system message states the model retrieves similar titles from the TMDB dataset and then answers, setting user expectations that answers are grounded in retrieved movie records.
